data.name: Benjamim
data.gender_notes: Benjamim is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Hebrew, Benjamim means 'son of the right hand' of a man. This name is derived from the Hebrew roots ben (son) and yamin (right hand). In the Bible, Benjam is a son of Jacob and one of the twelve tribes of Israel. The name Benjamim carries the meaning “Son of the right hand” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Benjamim usually hope their child will grow to embody son of the right hand and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbol of strength, protection, and being a faithful son.
data.etymology: Benjamim belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Son of the right hand.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Benjamim total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

in_english.name: Benjamim
in_english.meaning: son of the right hand, son of strength, son of blessing
in_english.long_meaning: Benjamim is a Hebrew name, meaning son of the right hand, son of strength, son of blessing. In Christian tradition, this name is significant for its biblical roots in Genesis and the New Testament, specifically in the Gospel of Matthew, where Benjamin is depicted as a righteous and blessed son of Jacob.

data.cultural_impact: The name Benjamim carries the rich history of the Israelite tribe and the spirit of ancient Hebrew culture. This name was traditionally given to boys in Jewish communities, reflecting their connection to their ancestral roots. It continues to be a popular name in Jewish and Christian communities around the world.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name Benjamim is deeply rooted in the concept of being a beloved child of God. The Hebrew word 'ben' means 'son', reminding us of the unconditional love and protection God has for us as His children. The 'yamin' part of the name symbolizes God's righteousness and strength being present with and bestowed upon us, as His right hand represents His guidance and support. Thus, the name Benjamim is a reminder of the comforting truth that God is always with us, and we are His prized possession, children of His right hand.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Benjamim, meaning "son of the right hand," symbolizes God's favor and blessing. In the Old Testament, Benjamin was the youngest but favored son of Jacob, reflecting God's love for those who are often overlooked or considered less significant.

biblical_reference.note: Benjamin is the youngest son of Jacob and Rachel, and is mentioned in the Bible as a righteous and blessed individual.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Benjamin was a son of Jacob and Rachel in the Hebrew Bible. The name Benjamim carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
